title: Uncovering hidden druggable sites: computational approaches to allosteric and cryptic pocket discovery-from molecular dynamics to AI.
authors: Lakkaraju, Sirish Kaushik; Pierce, Olivia; Mentes, Ahmet; Zhang, Ivy; Tokarski, John; Chalkley, Matthew; Kuriappan, Jissy; Mukherjee, Goutam; Palmeri, Antonio; Johnson, Theresa; Shanmugasundaram, Veerabahu
one_liner_zh: 该综述系统梳理了从分子动力学到AI/ML（如PocketMiner、AlphaFold3）的变构和隐蔽口袋计算方法，虽为综述且对象偏向药物发现，但核心聚焦蛋白质结构中的隐蔽位点识别，对蛋白质结构计算建模有直接参考价值。
abstract: Allosteric and cryptic binding pockets represent a vast underexploited frontier in drug discovery, offering routes to biological targets historically considered undruggable. The absence of apparent binding pockets in the global conformations of apo structures, together with limitations in availability of chemical probes and experimental structures for novel targets, makes the identification of allosteric and cryptic sites particularly challenging. Despite their ability to reveal transient and otherwise inaccessible pockets, computational methods remain underutilized for allosteric and cryptic site discovery. In this perspective, we present the current state-of-the-art of computational strategies that are available in a computational scientists' toolbox to evaluate the possibility of finding such pockets when assessing a new target in a drug discovery project. Computational approaches span a spectrum from physics-based methods grounded in molecular thermodynamics to AI/ML techniques for identifying allosteric and cryptic binding sites. Physics-based approaches encompass methods operating across multiple scales, from single-conformation analyses that identify pockets based on geometry and energetics (e.g., Fpocket, SiteMap) to molecular simulations that reveal cryptic states and transient binding sites, as well as mixed-solvent and probe-based approaches (e.g., SILCS, MixMD) that delineate druggable hotspots through enhanced sampling. AI/ML methods such as PocketMiner and deep learning cofolding models (AlphaFold3, Boltz) that rapidly predict cryptic sites are discussed in the context of them being over 1,000-fold faster than classical simulations. By surveying current methods and benchmark studies, we aim to define their domains of applicability, highlight their strengths and limitations, and identify opportunities for their integration in prospective drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 变构和隐蔽结合口袋代表了药物发现中一个尚未充分开发的广阔前沿，为历史上被认为不可成药的生物靶点提供了途径。脱辅基结构全局构象中缺乏明显的结合口袋，加上新型靶点的化学探针和实验结构可用性有限，使得变构和隐蔽位点的识别尤为具有挑战性。尽管计算方法能够揭示瞬态且其他方式无法触及的口袋，但在变构和隐蔽位点发现中仍未被充分利用。在本展望中，我们介绍了计算科学家工具箱中当前最先进的计算策略，以评估在药物发现项目中评估新靶点时发现此类口袋的可能性。计算方法涵盖从基于分子热力学的物理方法到用于识别变构和隐蔽结合位点的AI/ML技术。基于物理的方法包括跨多个尺度运作的手段，从基于几何和能量识别口袋的单构象分析（如Fpocket、SiteMap）到揭示隐蔽状态和瞬态结合位点的分子模拟，以及通过增强采样描绘可成药热点的混合溶剂和探针方法（如SILCS、MixMD）。AI/ML方法如PocketMiner和深度学习共折叠模型（AlphaFold3、Boltz）能够快速预测隐蔽位点，本文讨论了这些方法相较于经典模拟快逾1000倍的优势。通过调研现有方法和基准研究，我们旨在界定其适用领域，突出其优势与局限，并识别在前瞻性药物发现中整合这些方法的机会。
